API 510 vs 570 vs 653 Exam Pass Rates (2026): First-Time vs Overall ICP Data

Which API inspector exam is hardest? The pass-rate data answers clearly: API 570 (piping) has the highest first-time pass rate at roughly 56%, API 510 (pressure vessels) sits near 47%, and API 653 (storage tanks) is the toughest at approximately 38%. This analysis consolidates ICP statistics, training-provider aggregations, and Atlantis NDT cohort tracking for the 2024–2026 exam windows into one comparison — first-time vs overall rates, scoring math, study-hour benchmarks, and the body-of-knowledge sections that cause the most failures.

Why API ICP Pass Rates Are So Low

Three deliberate psychometric choices keep pass rates at 35–60%: (1) anti-cramming architecture — questions require integrating multiple code sections (a vessel-interval question may combine ASME VIII, API 510, and API 579), so memorization alone fails; (2) aggressive time pressure — roughly 1.7 minutes per closed-book question; and (3) statistically validated distractors built from real technician misconceptions, eliminating the lucky-guess floor. The difficulty is the credential: it underpins the $20,000–$35,000 annual salary premium API inspectors command.

First-Time vs Overall: Don't Be Fooled by the Blended Number

Marketing copy quotes “overall” rates of 65–75% without noting they include retakes. Plan against the first-time number: 47% for 510, 56% for 570, 38% for 653. Retake attempts pass at only 58–67% — roughly a third of retakers fail again, usually because they re-studied the same way instead of targeting the sections their diagnostic report flagged.

Body-of-Knowledge Failure Gates

Each exam has one or two sections that disproportionately sink candidates. API 510: Welding (ASME Section IX) and NDE Methods — candidates without hands-on welding/NDT backgrounds bleed points here. API 570: In-Service Inspection of Piping Systems (about 30% of the exam), which demands integrating ASME B31.3 with API 570 intervals and corrosion-rate math. API 653: Fitness-for-Service per API 579 and Tank Repair/Alteration — multi-step engineering calculations under time pressure, the main reason 653 is the hardest of the three.

The relationship is non-linear because open-book success depends on reference-navigation fluency, not just knowledge. Ignore “pass in 50 hours” claims — plan 250–400 hours over 12–16 weeks, with the final stretch devoted to full-length timed practice exams.

Scoring Math and Retake Policy

All three exams need 70% combined: roughly 105 of 150 correct for API 510, 91 of 130 for API 570, and 77 of 110 for API 653 (Modified Angoff equating shifts the raw cutscore slightly each window; there is no per-section minimum). Fail, and a strict 30-day waiting period applies before the next attempt, with a three-attempt cap per application window and a diagnostic report showing which BoK areas dropped you below the bar — spend 80% of retake study time on those bottom-quartile sections.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the API 510 exam pass rate in 2026?

Approximately 45–50% first-time (consensus ~47%), rising to 65–72% when retakes are included. The main failure gates are Welding (ASME Section IX) and NDE Methods, and inadequate study time under 200 hours.

What is the API 570 exam pass rate?

Approximately 55–60% first-time (~56%) — the highest of the three — and 70–78% overall. API 570's body of knowledge anchors on a single primary code (ASME B31.3), making it the recommended first exam of the three.

What is the API 653 pass rate, and why is it lowest?

Approximately 35–42% first-time (~38%), 55–65% overall. API 653 spans three code volumes — API 650, API 653, and API 579 — and its fitness-for-service calculations demand multi-step engineering math under closed-book time pressure.

How many correct answers do I need to pass?

70% combined across both sections: roughly 105/150 for API 510, 91/130 for API 570, and 77/110 for API 653, with the raw cutscore statistically equated a few questions either way each window.

How many study hours does a first-time pass take?

Most successful first-time passers report 250–350 focused hours over three to six months, with the final 50 hours on full-length timed practice exams. Under 50 hours, pass probability collapses below 15%.

In what order should I take the Triple Crown?

API 570 first (highest pass rate, builds confidence and open-book fluency), then API 510, then API 653 last — the sequence nearly all successful Triple Crown holders recommend.
